name: Stress-Split Bimetric MOND (SSBM)
claimed_mechanism: The MOND force law is sourced by the ghost-free massive-graviton helicity-0 mode of the h-metric, which couples to matter stress. The lensing slip (Phi != Psi) is generated by the quadrupolar (spin-2) component of the h-metric's nonlocal interaction. Because the slip is sourced by the stress tensor rather than a preferred frame, the PPN parameters are generated independently of the MOND screening factor, satisfying the A3 principle.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak field, the MOND dynamics are recovered via the nonlocal F+ operator acting on the h-metric. The lensing slip is proportional to the spin-2 component of the h-metric, which is finite in the high-acceleration limit (y >> 1). The PPN parameters are determined by the massive-graviton mass, not the MOND screening, avoiding the P7 collision.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-preferred-frame) because it uses a second metric (h) and nonlocality. It is inequivalent to DC-013 (slip-lock) because the slip is sourced by the stress tensor of the h-metric, not a frame. It is inequivalent to DC-014 (stiff vector) because there is no preferred-frame vector; the slip is generated by the spin-2 component of the h-metric.
